texts: mixed: everything the sentence says is present and the rule fires, but the term "cold-threshold stretches" packs one compound inside another ("cold-threshold" is itself two words modifying "stretches"), and the translator unpacked the inner half a second time, adding a stray claim that a cold threshold is a kind of threshold — an atom nothing else in the parse uses, and one it did not add for the very same phrase in your next sentence, so the wording is a coin-flip rather than reliably safe. Keep the modifier to one word and put the threshold in its own sentence: "Keepers forecast cold stretches from the spire weathercocks." plus "A stretch counts as cold when the cold reaches the threshold." — nothing is lost, and each half lands in a shape the translator handles the same way every time.
